title: Review: your third week, from curve shapes to your two trades
story: Friday evening, week three. Sam pins the two trade tickets, Cargo NS-01 and TTF-Q1, above your screen. *"Tonight, no new words. Six lessons, one picture. Then do what you will do every evening from now on: look at your two trades and tell me what changed."* Robin pulls up a chair to listen.
objective: I can connect the six lessons of week three and use them to check the two story trades.

write.heading: 1. The week in six lines
write.body:
- **L15**: contango (later prices higher) and backwardation (later prices lower) (→ L15).
- **L16**: spread = price A − price B; time, location, quality (→ L16).
- **L17**: crack, spark and dark spreads = margin of a plant (→ L17).
- **L18**: exchange (cleared, standard) vs OTC (bilateral, tailored); brokers (→ L18).
- **L19**: tankers, charters, Worldscale, demurrage (→ L19).
- **L20**: Cargo NS-01 and TTF-Q1, our two trades (→ L20).

write.heading: 2. Mini case: what changed tonight?
write.body:
Example (illustrative numbers):
- The TTF Q1 tenor moves from 37 to 36 EUR/MWh. MtM of TTF-Q1 = (36 − 35) × 90,000 = **+90,000 EUR**, down 90,000 since yesterday.
- The ship of Cargo NS-01 waits 2 days more than laytime at 40,000 USD/day: demurrage = **80,000 USD**, a new cost in the cargo P&L.
- The 600 Brent futures are on ICE: cleared, so margin is paid every day, no credit risk on a counterparty.

write.heading: 3. Your evening questions
write.body: Which tenor and which source did I use? Are all costs in (freight, demurrage)? Exchange or OTC: who is the counterparty?

check.q: The curve is 80 for M1 and 83 for M3. Contango or backwardation? What is the M1-M3 spread?
check.a: Contango: later prices are higher. M1 − M3 = 80 − 83 = −3 (L15, L16; illustrative numbers).

check.q: Power 100 EUR/MWh, gas 35, efficiency means 2 MWh of gas per MWh of power, 0.4 t CO2 per MWh at 70 EUR/t. Clean spark spread?
Why do the 600 Brent futures of Cargo NS-01 carry no counterparty credit risk for Northbridge?
check.a: They are exchange-traded and cleared: the clearing house stands between buyer and seller, and margin is paid every day (L18).

check.q: Name two costs that must appear in the P&L of Cargo NS-01 besides the crude price.
check.a: Freight (the cost of the ship) and demurrage if the ship waits longer than laytime (L19, L20).

read_more: Flip back through L15 to L20 while you copy: each (→ L<n>) mark is a page to reread. All prices, days and rates are illustrative and Northbridge is fictional. This is the last lesson of module 2 (markets and prices). Module 3 starts next: the instruments themselves, beginning with the physical contract behind Cargo NS-01. Notice how the mini case already mixes the three things you will check every evening: the price (curve tenor and source), the costs (freight, demurrage) and the counterparty (exchange or OTC).
next: Next lesson (L22): module 3 starts with the physical contract behind Cargo NS-01: term vs spot, and the key clauses.
